person.bibl: Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952.
person.note: Received 3 shares of Thiruvisannalur, for he had mastered 3 śāstras. See Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 38–39.

Periappā Kavi mentions him in the prologue to his Śṛṇgāramañjarī-Śāhajīya as one of the most celebrated poets of the time. See Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 43.

While V. Raghavan claims that the Jīvānandananāṭaka and Vidyāpariṇayanāṭaka are 'really the work of Vedakavi' (see Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 29), others claim that there is no evidence to this effect and prefer to attribute the authorship to Ānandarāyamakhin. See entry on Jīvānandananāṭaka for further details.
For the alternative name Vedakavi Svāmin, see New Catalogus Catalogurum (NCC). Vols 1-36: vol. 31, p. 147.
